one_liner: A senior supervisory health-administration role at ICE's Health Service Corps, overseeing detention health operations, accreditation compliance and contracts, filled only by commissioned USPHS officers.
fit_summary: This billet is open only to current U.S. Public Health Service commissioned officers at the O-6 level, and Call to Active Duty candidates are excluded, so Daniel is not eligible as a civilian. It also requires five years each of leadership, program management and personnel management as a uniformed service officer, plus correctional health experience. Daniel's emergency-management consulting background touches on the COOP and emergency response duties, but it cannot overcome the eligibility barrier.
eligibility: Only current USPHS commissioned officers may apply; USPHS Call to Active Duty candidates are not eligible, and civilians cannot apply despite the 'public' hiring path tag.
The billet is O-6 (CC-6), and it requires five years each of leadership, program/services management and personnel management experience as a uniformed service officer.
Correctional health experience is required; a master's degree in healthcare administration or a related health field is preferred.
You must be able to obtain and keep a DHS Secret clearance, earn Level II COR certification within 12 months, and hold CPR/BLS certification.
You must meet physical demands, including jogging or fast-walking 1/4 mile, lifting over 30 pounds, and performing CPR.
strategy: Do not apply to this posting. Your application would be screened out because you are not a current USPHS officer.

Use the posting's language (COOP, ERG, Sit Reps, taskings, stakeholder liaison) to frame your IEM work on your two-page resume for civilian roles such as FEMA or DHS emergency management specialist, program analyst or COR-track positions.

Search USAJOBS for 'open to the public' FEMA, ICE or DHS positions in the GS-9 to GS-12 range, depending on your actual experience. Also check Virginia VDEM and Prince William County or Manassas emergency management jobs closer to home.
Describe your IEM work in terms of client agencies supported, preparedness or recovery deliverables, and hours per week, filling in only facts you can verify.
Consider earning a FAC-COR Level I certification and completing FEMA IS-100/200/700/800 courses. Both are low-cost credentials that match the keywords in this posting.
resume_bullets: Supported [client agency] [preparedness/recovery] program at IEM, coordinating [number] stakeholders and preparing [Sit Reps/status reports] for [audience]; [hours] hrs/week, [dates].
Contributed to [COOP/emergency operations plan] development for [client], reviewing [policies/procedures] for compliance with [standard] and recommending [changes].
Served as liaison between [client] and [vendors/partners], tracking [deliverables/invoices] against [contract requirements] to resolve [issue type].
interview_questions: Describe a time you ensured a program complied with complex policies or accreditation standards.
How have you supported continuity of operations or emergency response planning?
Tell us about managing competing tasking deadlines across multiple stakeholders.
How do you identify and resolve discrepancies in contractor performance or invoices?
watch_outs: This posting is restricted to USPHS officers only, so you are ineligible.
It requires correctional health experience and five years of uniformed-officer management experience.
It involves up to 30% travel, 24/7 availability and physical demands.
The listed salary data ($1 to $150,000) is unreliable because uniformed service pay follows the commissioned corps pay scale.
